# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Champion is cand_0001 (val 0.600). cand_0002 was REJECTED and reverted (its reopen-and-revert
checklist broke 30709/59259; its split-stays-text edit broke 58147). Diagnosed all 20 failing
trajectories via 4 parallel read-only subagents (groups A–D), separated environment faults and
inconsistent-gold from prompt-fixable knowledge gaps, then shipped 4 additive/narrowed prose
edits — all in task_template.md, all in the SAME direction as cand_0001's accepted type/literal
rules and deliberately distinct from the two refuted cand_0002 edits.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by leverage; biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | tag | fixable? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Formula that references dynamic-array-spilled cells (UNIQUE/SORT/…) can't recalc → #N/A error string; agent even had the literal solution and switched to a formula | 38332 | KNOWLEDGE | YES → Edit A |
| 2 | Correct value stored as TEXT after a COPY/TRANSPOSE (agent assumed relocation preserves type) | 56427 (14 cells str-not-float) | KNOWLEDGE (extends accepted rule) | YES → Edit C |
| 3 | "Standardize/reformat into dd/mm/yy" written as a text string; gold is a real datetime | 51958 | KNOWLEDGE | YES → Edit B |
| 4 | Invented "#N/A" for unmatched rows the instruction never described as error-valued (gold wanted a real int) | 55931 | KNOWLEDGE (narrows named-literal rule) | PARTIAL → Edit D |
| — | ENVIRONMENT FAULTS (handed back, NOT prompt defects) | 73-45, 56996, 47741 | — | NO |
| — | INCONSISTENT-GOLD (gold contradicts stated instruction / worked example) | 50630, 5192, 59743, 450-9 | — | NO |
| — | LOGIC/AMBIGUITY (multiple valid solutions / underspecified) | 11842, 325-44, 39046, 3911, 53367, 56637, 57090, 57232, 51359 | — | NO (regression risk / not a knowledge gap) |

## Changes made this iteration (all task_template.md)
| edit | cluster | lever (SKILL type) | what & why it generalizes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 38332 | Add missing rule (KNOWLEDGE) | "A formula that references dynamic-array-spilled cells (UNIQUE/SORT/FILTER/SEQUENCE/spilling XLOOKUP) can't be recalculated → #N/A; when the answer is a plain value, compute the literal in Python even if the instruction says 'create a formula'. CF/format rules exempt." |
| B | 51958 | Add missing rule (KNOWLEDGE) | "A request to convert/standardize/reformat a value INTO a date/time pattern means the target holds a real datetime and the pattern is applied via number_format — not a text string." |
| C | 56427 | Consolidate/extend accepted rule | "Type-matching applies even when COPYING/TRANSPOSING/RELOCATING a value: convert numeric/date-looking text to the destination column's numeric/date type; keep genuine text columns as text." |
| D | 55931 | Narrowing rule (adds discriminating condition) | "Write an Excel error literal or dash placeholder ONLY when the instruction names it or a worked-example cell shows it; never invent it for an unmatched case — a missing lookup value is a method bug to fix." |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per edit; evidence from traces)
- Edit A → trace 38332: agent wrote `=IF(COUNTIF($A$2:$A$18,C2)>0,1,0)` where C2:C5 is a `=_xlfn.UNIQUE(_xlfn._xlws.SORT(...))` spill; grader: "4 cells hold an Excel error text … str where int was expected." The agent had computed the literal ints earlier then abandoned them because the instruction said "create a formula." New rule tells it to keep the literal in exactly this spill-reference case → cells become the expected int. SAFE: condition = "formula references SPILLED cells AND answer is a plain value"; passing formula-answer tasks (58047, 55609, 56975, 58109) reference normal cells and recalc fine, so untouched; CF task CF_11072 explicitly exempted.
- Edit B → trace 51958: agent wrote `ws["B2"] = "09/08/21 10:06"` (str); grader: "str where datetime was expected — write the real typed value." Rule now maps "standardize into dd/mm/yy" to a typed datetime + number_format → type matches. SAFE: narrow trigger ("convert/standardize/reformat INTO a date/time pattern"); does NOT fire on split-into-parts tasks (50630) or on date-looking text pass-throughs, so it doesn't touch that class.
- Edit C → trace 56427: agent transposed column-G strings ('1.3','5.5') into H:S verbatim; grader: "14 cells hold the CORRECT value stored as text instead of as a number … str where float was expected." Rule extends the accepted text→number rule to the relocate/transpose case → values written as float. SAFE: scoped to "destination column's expected type is numeric/date"; explicit carve-out keeps text/ID/code columns as strings.
- Edit D → trace 55931: agent wrote `target.value = "#N/A"` for 8 unmatched songs; grader: "8 cells hold an Excel error text … str where int was expected." Rule forbids inventing error literals the instruction never named and redirects to fixing the method. SAFE/ADDITIVE-NARROWING: it does NOT loosen the existing "if the instruction NAMES the literal, write it" rule (57232-style tasks that name #N/A still write it); it only forbids fabricating an unrequested error string.

## Blast-radius per edit
- Edit A: BOUNDED — additive, condition-gated (formula references spilled cells AND answer is a value); passing formula/CF tasks excluded by construction.
- Edit B: BOUNDED — additive; narrow trigger (explicit reformat-INTO-date wording); same direction as the accepted cand_0001 text→date rule.
- Edit C: BOUNDED — additive extension of the already-accepted openpyxl-str rule, in the same direction, with a text-column carve-out.
- Edit D: BOUNDED — additive NARROWING that constrains error-literal invention; the permissive "named literal → write it" rule is preserved untouched.

## Refuted edits I did NOT re-try (from cand_0002 RESULT broke={30709,58147,59259})
- The "reopen the ORIGINAL input and revert any overwritten cell" pre-finish checklist (broke leave-untouched tasks 30709/59259) — NOT re-added; left cand_0001's simpler leave-untouched rule as-is.
- The blanket "split/extract substrings stay TEXT" default (implicated in breaking 58147) — NOT re-added. Edit B is the opposite (reformat-INTO-date) and is narrowly triggered, so it does not resurrect that regressor.

## Process & features used
- Subagents: 4 parallel general-purpose read-only subagents (groups A–D) diagnosed all 20 failing
  traces with quoted grader evidence; I synthesized clusters and applied edits serially.
- Prior iterations read: cand_0001 (accepted) diff+PROCESS, cand_0002 (rejected) diff+PROCESS,
  LEDGER, JOURNAL, RUNMAP.

## Good things to PRESERVE
- Did NOT touch the bidirectional "named literal (#N/A / '-') → write that exact literal" rule.
- Did NOT add the reopen-and-revert checklist or the split-stays-text default (both refuted).
- Did NOT strengthen the leave-untouched rule (already present; pushing it harder broke 30709/59259).

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- 73-45, 56996, 47741 — ENVIRONMENT faults (grader-flagged recalc failure / volatile RANDBETWEEN
  source / TEXTJOIN+TEXT+WORKDAY recalc-to-error). Prose can't fix a broken/volatile recalc; a
  literal workaround was refuted in a prior run and the tasks explicitly require a formula.
- 50630, 5192, 59743, 450-9 — INCONSISTENT-GOLD: the gold contradicts the stated instruction or a
  visible worked-example cell (50630 example is a datetime but gold wants text; 5192's two examples
  contradict each other and the gold; 59743's gold drops the F−J clause the instruction states;
  450-9's label type is int-in-example but str-in-gold). No prose rule recovers these without
  hardcoding the answer or regressing the class.
- 11842, 325-44, 39046, 3911, 53367, 56637, 57090, 57232, 51359 — LOGIC/AMBIGUITY: near-misses or
  multiple-valid-solution / underspecified logic (half-day model, bespoke filter grammar, note
  allocation, unique-count formula quirk, multi-column intent, over-matched lookup, pre-filled
  inconsistent given cell). 51359 in particular is the leave-untouched cluster whose stronger
  enforcement already regressed passing tasks — not re-attempted.
